GENERATE BURST VF-prim-fire-sheet-01 — painted primitive P07 FLAME SHEET — the wake body of a fire bolt in flight for the fire treatment (Run C-5, E1: the fire projectile; architecture 03- § 2.3 build list). task_id "VF-prim-fire-sheet-01". One primitive per call. Paint the SHAPE REPRESENTING EMISSION only — light, glow, colour and motion are runtime layers.

IMAGE 1 is the SCALE + REGISTER board: a 1:1 native 512×512 crop of the painted cliffside clearing at the game camera with two figures 130 px tall (= 1 BH, body height) beside a 3× enlargement; everything is hand-drawn painted 2D — confident dark contour with taper, clean painted planes, restrained texture. IMAGE 2 is the APPROVED fire impact peak (E0-p; Matt-accepted): the fire VOCABULARY to match exactly — four flat greyscale value planes (near-black contour/rim, dark grey outer flame, light grey mid flame, white core), hooked tongues with hard plane edges, no gradients or glow. IMAGE 3 is the native ground crop alone (reading only).

Deliver EXACTLY ONE image, 512×512, GENUINELY TRANSPARENT background (RGBA: alpha 0 outside the body, opaque inside, no soft fringe wider than 1 px) — if transparency is impossible, a flat uniform #00ff00 plate and SAY SO. Content: a FLAME SHEET — the trailing body of a fire bolt in flight (its wake), travelling to the RIGHT: a broad ragged sheet of flame streaming LEFT from an unseen head on the right, about 2.2 BH long (≈ 290 px) and 0.9 BH tall (≈ 115 px) at its widest near the right end, thinning and breaking into three or four separated hooked wisps at the far left; the sheet is FULLER than a streak — a body of fire, not a line — with a light-grey mid plane filling most of it and a white plane only near the right end where it meets the head; hand-drawn dark contour with taper; asymmetric top-to-bottom. FOUR flat greyscale planes, hard-edged, no glow. Centred; nothing touches the edge. Deliver: out/fire_sheet_01.png.
RETURN: the receipt (task_id "VF-prim-fire-sheet-01"): images = integer; calls_used; status; concerns honestly.
